# Geofence fairness eval

This is a simulated measurement of the clock-in geofence rule, not field data.
At 300 ft under tree cover, a strict fence (`strict`) wrongly flags 10.5% of workers who are on site; the shipped rule (`fair`) wrongly flags 0.1%.
In a hollow at 300 ft it is 28.1% for `strict` and 0.2% for `fair`.
The price: in a hollow at 300 ft, `fair` passes 77.0% of people standing 1.5 x the radius away as on site (`strict` 5.8%, the candidate `capped` 74.5%).
The worst case for `fair` is hollow at 150 ft: 93.2% of people standing 1.5 x the radius away pass as on site.

## What this is and is not

Everything here is simulated from a seeded random generator (seed 20261118, 20000 trials per row). It is not field data, and no real location was used.
The error model below is a set of assumptions about how phones behave. The real fixes from the beta replace these assumptions (M2.6).

How the simulation works:
- The phone reports a stated accuracy in meters. By the W3C Geolocation spec that is a 95% confidence radius.
- The position error is a 2-D Gaussian, so the error distance follows a Rayleigh curve. Sigma is set so that 95% of error distances fall within stated accuracy x honesty (sigma = that distance / 2.4477).
- Honesty is the true 95% error divided by the stated accuracy. 1 is an honest phone; 3 means the real error is 3 times what the phone claims.
- A worker who is on site stands at a random spot inside the fence circle (even by area). A person who is off site stands 1.5 x the radius, 3 x the radius, 1 mile (1609 m) from the pin, at a random bearing.
- Distances are flat-earth meters, which is fine at these scales.
- Every policy is run on the same simulated fixes, so the rows compare like with like.

| Environment | What it stands for | Stated accuracy (m) | Honesty |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open_sky` | Open sky, good GPS lock | 4 to 12 | 1 |
| `tree_cover` | Under tree cover | 15 to 45 | 1 |
| `hollow` | Steep hollow, few satellites in view | 40 to 120 | 1 |
| `overconfident` | Cheap phone that claims a better fix than it has (multipath) | 8 to 20 | 3 |
| `cell_only` | No GPS lock, cell towers only | 300 to 1500 | 1 |

| Policy | What it does |
|---|---|
| `strict` | What most time clocks do: on site only if the reported spot is inside the circle. |
| `fair` | The shipped rule (`Geo.fenceStatus` in `js/geo.ts`): the stated accuracy is subtracted from the distance first. |
| `capped` | A candidate, not shipped: like `fair`, but the amount subtracted is never more than the radius. |

What the results mean for a clock-in. Nothing is ever blocked.
- Clean: the rule says on site.
- Wrongly flagged: the worker is on site but the boss sees a "near" or "off site" flag. This is the unfair outcome.
- Photo asked: the fix is too weak to judge (stated accuracy worse than 152 m), so the worker is asked for a photo instead.
- Passed as on site: the person is not there but the punch looks clean. This is the missed outcome.

    npm run eval:geofence                       # rewrite this report and geofence.json
    node evals/geofence/run.mts --check         # fail if the committed files are out of date

## What it says about the rule

- **On-site workers are treated fairly when the phone is honest.** Across `open_sky`, `tree_cover`, `hollow` and all 3 radii, `fair` wrongly flags at most 0.6% of on-site workers (hollow, 150 ft). `strict` wrongly flags up to 51.3% (hollow, 150 ft).
- **The rule is only as fair as the phone is honest.** In `overconfident`, where the real error is 3 times the stated accuracy, `fair` wrongly flags 4.8% of on-site workers at 300 ft (`strict` 14.9%), and up to 9.9% at 150 ft.
- **The worst false pass for `fair`** is hollow at 150 ft: 93.2% of people standing 1.5 x the radius away pass as on site. On the same cell `strict` passes 14.1% and `capped` passes 70.1%.
- **Where the shipped rule is weak.** A big stated accuracy on a small fence lets a person who is close but not there pass as on site. The stated accuracy can be as large as 152 m before a photo is asked for, and the smallest fence is 46 m, so the benefit of the doubt can be up to 3.3 times the fence itself. In 3 of the 45 off-site rows, `fair` passes more than half of the people who are not there. The 6 worst rows for `fair`, with the other two policies on the same simulated fixes:

| Environment | Fence | True distance | `strict` passes | `fair` passes | `capped` passes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hollow` | 150 ft | 1.5 x the radius | 14.1% | 93.2% | 70.1% |
| `hollow` | 300 ft | 1.5 x the radius | 5.8% | 77.0% | 74.5% |
| `tree_cover` | 150 ft | 1.5 x the radius | 2.9% | 61.5% | 61.5% |
| `hollow` | 600 ft | 1.5 x the radius | 0.6% | 33.9% | 33.9% |
| `hollow` | 150 ft | 3 x the radius | 0.4% | 31.2% | 6.3% |
| `overconfident` | 150 ft | 1.5 x the radius | 6.5% | 24.1% | 24.1% |

- **`capped` compared with `fair`.** The two differ in 2 of the 15 environment and fence pairs (hollow at 150 ft, hollow at 300 ft) and give the same numbers everywhere else, because the cap only matters when the stated accuracy is larger than the radius.
  - hollow at 150 ft: false passes at 1.5 x the radius go from 93.2% to 70.1% (23.1 points lower), and on-site workers wrongly flagged go from 0.6% to 8.8% (8.2 points higher).
  - hollow at 300 ft: false passes at 1.5 x the radius go from 77.0% to 74.5% (2.5 points lower), and on-site workers wrongly flagged go from 0.2% to 0.4% (0.2 points higher).
  - On the worst cell for `fair` (hollow, 150 ft, 1.5 x the radius), `capped` still passes 70.1%, and it wrongly flags 8.8% of on-site workers where `fair` flags 0.6%. The cap trades some fairness for fewer false passes; it does not remove the weakness.
- **Far away is caught.** Across every environment and fence, `fair` passes at most 0.0% of people who are 1 mile away. `strict` passes up to 0.04% (cell_only, 600 ft), because it trusts a fix that has no GPS lock.
- **A weak fix becomes a photo, not a flag.** In `cell_only`, `fair` asks at least 100.0% of on-site workers for a photo and flags 0.0%. `strict` wrongly flags up to 98.7% of them (150 ft).
- **Photo friction stays where it belongs.** In the other environments (`open_sky`, `tree_cover`, `hollow`, `overconfident`), `fair` asks at most 0.0% of on-site workers for a photo.

## Decision

The shipped rule is unchanged by this eval. This report measures `Geo.fenceStatus` as it is; it does not change it.
Whether to change it (for example to `capped`) is a product decision, and it is logged in HANDOFF.md.
